w: The South Tyrol Museum of Archaeology in Bolzano is built around one extraordinary resident: the preserved body of Otzi the Iceman. It is the museum's defining exhibit, the reason a South Tyrolean archaeological collection is known well beyond the region, drawing visitors to this otherwise modest city institution.
s: The museum built around Otzi the Iceman's body
_facts: Archaeological museum in Bolzano, South Tyrol
Home of the preserved body of Otzi the Iceman

w: Bolzano's Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art takes its name from the Greek for temple of the muses. Founded 1985, it moved in 2008 into a new building by Berlin firm KSV - Kruger Schuberth Vandreike - in the centre of town, run since 2006 by a foundation backed by the Province and Museion Association.
s: A temple of the muses in a striking 2008 building
_facts: Founded 1985; name from Greek for temple of the muses
New venue by KSV architects opened 24 May 2008 in central Bolzano
Run since 2006 by the Museion Foundation

w: In 1237 the Prince-Bishop of Trent, Alderich, granted the brothers Friedrich and Beral, Lords of Wangen, permission to build a castle on a rocky spur then known as Runchenstayn. That medieval fortification, now called Runkelstein - or Castel Roncolo in Italian - still stands above the Ritten territory near Bolzano.
s: A 1237 castle built on a rock called Runchenstayn
_facts: 1237: Prince-Bishop Alderich of Trent grants building permission
Built by brothers Friedrich and Beral, Lords of Wangen
Rock originally called Runchenstayn; near Bolzano in Ritten territory

w: Bolzano Cathedral - Maria Himmelfahrt, the Assumption of Mary - is the parish church of South Tyrol's capital and seat of the Diocese of Bozen-Brixen, though an odd split survives: the bishop has resided in Bozen since 1964, while the cathedral chapter stayed in Brixen, leaving two co-cathedrals sharing one diocese.
s: One diocese, two co-cathedrals, split since 1964
_facts: Parish church of Bolzano, cathedral of Diocese of Bozen-Brixen
Bishop has resided in Bozen since 1964
Cathedral chapter remains in Brixen; co-cathedral with Brixen Cathedral

w: One of Tyrol's earliest Gothic buildings, this church was built by Dominican friars from 1272 outside the old walls - the quarter grew into Bolzano's Neustadt. Wartime bombs damaged it badly, but frescoes survive: a 1404 Madonna and Saints by Hans Stotzinger, and a Giottoesque cycle in the Chapel of St John.
s: A 1272 Gothic church that gave Bolzano its Neustadt
_facts: Built by Dominicans, completed 1272; early Tyrolean Gothic architecture
Gave its name to the Neustadt quarter of Bolzano
Heavily damaged by WWII bombs
1404 fresco Madonna and Saints by Hans Stotzinger; Giottoesque Four Horsemen cycle in St John's Chapel

w: Built to co-host the 1994 Men's World Ice Hockey Championships alongside Milan's Forum di Assago, this 7,200-seat arena has gone by PalaOnda and Eiswelle. It is home ice for HC Bolzano and the EVB Eagles Sudtirol, and has staged the 1998 European Handball Championships and a CEV volleyball final four.
s: A 1994 world-championship arena, still home ice today
_facts: Built for 1994 Men's World Ice Hockey Championships; 7,200 capacity
Formerly PalaOnda / Eiswelle
Home of HC Bolzano and EVB Eagles Sudtirol (EWHL)
Hosted 1998 European Handball Championships and 2010-11 CEV Champions League final four

w: These late-medieval fortifications near Bolzano - Castel Firmiano in Italian - stood as ruins until 2006, when Reinhold Messner opened the fourth of his Mountain Museums inside them. MMM Firmian, opened 9 June 2006, turns the castle into a mountaineering museum, mixing medieval stone with Messner's collection.
s: A ruined castle turned into Messner's mountain museum
_facts: Extensive Late Middle Ages fortifications near Bolzano, aka Castel Firmiano
Ruins house the fourth Messner Mountain Museum (MMM Firmian)
MMM opened 9 June 2006, founded by Reinhold Messner
